No candidates may simply mean there is nothing to select or clean up. You do not need to create __pycache__ in a real project.

Check the selected path and analysis status first. Cancellation, read errors, or exclusions mean the absence of candidates is not conclusive. Check Errors & exclusions.

Even a completed analysis may find no cache matching the current rules. Folder sizes and Largest files remain available. Virtual environments, node_modules, and build outputs are review-only.

The test-project feature creates a new folder under your chosen parent, generates fixed source files and a real Python cache, then registers and analyzes it. It does not copy or overwrite existing files. Test data uses the same protection, content verification, environment tests, and explicit confirmation; it does not bypass execution qualification.

If creation fails or is cancelled, the new folder may contain partial test data; its path is displayed. It is not deleted automatically. Removing it from the list leaves the actual folder in place.

Logical file size confirmed recycled and observed free disk space are different values. The app does not empty the Recycle Bin, so immediate free-space growth is not guaranteed.

Failure or unconfirmed results do not prove success or source preservation. Check the original path and Windows Recycle Bin. After a journal error, stop further cleanup and restart after storage becomes writable, then inspect history.

To restore, open Windows Recycle Bin, match the original location and deletion time, then select Restore. The app does not restore automatically, empty the bin, or permanently delete files. It cannot recover an already emptied bin.

After a cleanup attempt, previous candidates cannot be reused until reanalysis. Passing environment tests does not prove every folder can be deleted; each candidate is revalidated immediately before execution.
